correctness.rationale: For a candidate fort F in a complete multipartite graph, an outside vertex in part i has exactly \(|F|-|F\cap X_i|\) neighbors in F. This condition immediately yields the complete minimal classification: same-part pairs in non-singleton parts, pairs of singleton vertices, and 3-part transversal triples with at most one singleton. The count formulas follow by choosing these edges. The fort-number formula is supported by the exchange normalization of triple forts and the parity-leftover argument; the fractional zero-forcing formula follows from all pair constraints and explicit half-weight feasible solutions (with the lone singleton weighted zero when q=1). A fresh definition-level brute-force replay through order 8 reproduced the entire minimal-fort hypergraph, edge counts and exact maximum matching for every part profile; the package also records a larger order-10 LP replay. Finite computation is corroborative only.

value.rationale: Minimal forts are the irredundant obstruction hyperedges underlying fort-cover formulations of zero forcing. Complete multipartite graphs are a canonical family, and the transition from pair-only bipartite forts to rank-3 transversal triples is structurally meaningful. The theorem simultaneously resolves the full minimal-fort hypergraph, its edge count, maximum disjoint-fort packing and fractional transversal number for every part profile, so it is mathematically useful rather than a routine finite enumeration.

limitations: Standard zero-forcing forts only; no claim for PSD/skew/other forcing rules.
Finite exhaustive replays are corroborative, not the universal proof.
